answer: Each paper mill registers the wire pattern of its watermark mould, and every sheet must show the mould that made it. A whisper sheet pressed on another mould fails the register: at the thread of the watermark the wires must match the mill's own pattern, and a strange sheet shows another mill's mark. Forging a mould means building a paper mill, hiring a vatman for a year and paying 18,900, and the velvet pattern in the register is checked at every sale, so a sheet whose mould was never registered is pulped.
